---
title: "Adding tables and figures"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# The pictures of this page's tables: committed in inst/rtf-examples/articles/
# (made by data-raw/gen_article_shots.R, which renders the page with
# RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT set, so .keep() writes the RTF) and copied next to
# the article to be served.
.here <- normalizePath(".")
.keep <- function(x, file) {
  out <- Sys.getenv("RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT")
  if (!nzchar(out)) return(invisible(NULL))
  doc <- if (inherits(x, "rtf_document")) x
         else if (inherits(x, "rtfplot")) rtfreporter::rtf_figures(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
         else rtfreporter::rtf_tables(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
  rtfreporter::generate_rtfreport(doc, file.path(out, file), overwrite = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
.shot <- function(file) {
  # the package's folder: the one above this page with a DESCRIPTION
  root <- .here
  while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION")) && dirname(root) != root) root <- dirname(root)
  src <- file.path(root, "inst", "rtf-examples", "articles", file)
  if (!file.exists(src)) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(file.path(.here, "figures", "articles"), showWarnings = FALSE,
             recursive = TRUE)
  file.copy(src, file.path(.here, "figures", "articles", file), overwrite = TRUE)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "articles", file), error = FALSE)
}
```

```{r setup, fold = FALSE}
library(rtfreporter)
```

A rtfreporter document is a **sequence of contents** -- tables and figures --
each with an optional title and footnote block. You add content with
`rtf_tables()` (and `rtf_figures()` for images); by default each element you
pass starts a page of its own, and `page_break = FALSE` puts it under the
content before it instead (see [Two contents on one page](#two-contents-on-one-page)).

This article is the deep dive on content. For document-wide settings (page size,
fonts) see [Page & document setup](page-setup.html); for converting `gt` /
`gtsummary` / `rtables` objects see
[Importing tables](importing-tables.html); for splitting a long table across
pages see [Paginating with as_rtftables()](pagination.html).

```{r data, fold = "closed"}
df1 <- data.frame(Parameter = c("Age", "  Mean", "  SD"),
                  Value     = c("", "75.1", "8.2"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df2 <- data.frame(Parameter = c("Sex", "  F", "  M"),
                  Value     = c("", "53%", "47%"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```


## A single table

The quickest way is to hand a data.frame straight to `rtf_tables()` -- a
single item needs no `list()`, and it gets the default look (TFL borders, the
first column left, the others centred):

```{r single-bare}
doc <- rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(df1)
length(doc$contents)        # one page
```

A table's appearance is written on the table: build it with `rtftable()` (or
`as_rtftables()` for gt/rtables sources, or a plan's `plan_style()`) and pass
that:

```{r single-built}
tbl <- rtftable(df1, border = "tfl", row_height_twips = 280L,
                col_rel_width = c(2, 1),
                col_spec = list(list(col = 2, align = "right")))
doc <- rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(tbl)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "ac_single.rtf")
.shot("ac_single.png")
```

The options (`border`, `col_rel_width`, `row_height_twips`, `col_spec`, ...)
are documented on `?rtftable`.  (`rtf_tables()` used to take copies of them;
those are deprecated and removed in 0.9.0.)

### Column alignment and `row_title`

By default the **row-heading column is left-aligned and every data column is
centred** — the usual clinical look. The heading column is the first one unless
you say otherwise with `row_title` (an integer vector of column indices or a
vector of column names):

```{r row-title}
# Columns 1-2 are row headings (left); columns 3+ are data (centre).
tbl <- rtftable(df1, row_title = c(1, 2))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(tbl, "ac_row_title.rtf")
.shot("ac_row_title.png")
```

`row_title` only sets the *default* alignment; an explicit `col_spec` `align`,
an `rtf_table_style`, or alignment read from a gt/rtables source still wins, and
column headers follow their column's data alignment. `as_rtftables()` takes
`row_title` too, so the same default applies to every page of a table.


## The same settings for several tables

Build every table with the same settings -- `lapply()` over the data.frames
-- and pass the list.  Each element becomes its own page:

```{r bulk}
pages <- lapply(list(df1, df2), rtftable,
                border = "tfl", row_height_twips = 280L, col_rel_width = c(2, 1))
doc <- rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(pages)
length(doc$contents)        # two pages, same look
```


## Different settings per table

When each table needs its own look, build each one separately (with its own
settings) and pass the list. Pre-built `rtftable()` objects keep their own
settings:

```{r individual}
t1 <- rtftable(df1, border = "tfl", row_height_twips = 280L)
t2 <- rtftable(df2, border = NULL,  row_height_twips = 200L)   # no borders

doc <- rtf_document() |> rtf_tables(list(t1, t2))
doc$contents[[1]]$content$row_height_twips   # 280 -- t1 keeps its own
doc$contents[[2]]$content$row_height_twips   # 200 -- t2 keeps its own
```



## Titles and footnotes

Each page can carry a title block and a footnote block. One block element becomes
one line. Title lines default to centred + bold; footnote lines default to left,
and the footnote's first line carries a top rule as the separator. Use `NULL` for
a page with none.

By default the **title** renders as plain **text paragraphs** spanning the
writable page width (so it is centred over the page), while the **footnote**
renders as a content-width single-column **table** (which carries the separator
rule). You can switch either form with the document defaults
`title_format` / `footnote_format` (`"text"` or `"table"`):

```{r title-format}
doc <- rtf_document(default_format = list(title_format = "table")) |>  # legacy
  rtf_tables(list(df1), titles = list("Table 14.1.1"))
```

Pass `titles` / `footnotes` as lists parallel to the content (one element per
page):

```{r titles}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(
    list(df1, df2),
    titles    = list(c("Table 14.1.1", "Demographics"),
                     c("Table 14.1.2", "Sex")),
    footnotes = list(c("Source: ADSL"), NULL)
  )
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "ac_titles_pages.rtf")
.shot("ac_titles_pages.png")
```

### Common (one block for every page)

If you pass a **length-1** list, that single block is applied to every page --
handy for a footnote that repeats on all pages:

```{r titles-common}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(list(df1, df2),
             footnotes = list(c("Confidential", "Source: ADSL")))   # on both pages
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "ac_titles_common.rtf")
.shot("ac_titles_common.png")
```

### Styling

A **title** block can be a plain character vector (default styling) **or** a
list of rows, where each row is a string or a styled list with any of `align`,
`bold`, `italic`, `underline` and `color` (a `"#RRGGBB"` hex).

A **footnote** is styled as a block, with [rtf_footnotes()]: `align`,
`font_size_half_points`, `markup`, and `border` (an [rtf_border()], e.g. the
rule above it). A footnote row may be `c(l = , c = , r = )`, up to three cells
on one line -- the source on the left and the run date on the right:

```{r titles-styled}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(
    list(df1),
    titles = list(list(
      "Table 14.1.1",
      list(text = "Provisional", italic = TRUE, color = "#C00000")
    ))
  ) |>
  rtf_footnotes(list(list(c(l = "Source: ADSL", r = "Run: {DATETIME:%Y-%m-%d}"))),
                border = rtf_border(top = TRUE))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "ac_titles.rtf")
.shot("ac_titles.png")
```

You can also set blocks after the content with `rtf_titles()` /
`rtf_footnotes()` (both accept a per-page list or a single common block). When
the content comes from a `gt` table via `as_rtftables()`, its title and source
notes flow through automatically -- see
[Importing tables](importing-tables.html).


## Cell-text markup

Cell text (data cells, column / spanning headers, titles and footnotes) is run
through a small markup step controlled by the `markup` argument of `rtftable()`
(and `rtf_tables()` for bare data.frames; the document-wide default is
`rtf_document(default_format = list(markup = ))`). It takes a character vector of:

- `"script"` -- `^{...}` renders as superscript, `_{...}` as subscript (this is
  how adapter-generated footnote reference marks such as `^{1}` become real
  superscripts);
- `"relational"` -- the literal `">="` is converted to the `>=` symbol
  (U+2265) and `"<="` to `<=` (U+2264).

The default is **`"script"`** -- super/subscript on, but the `>=` / `<=` symbol
conversion **off**, so a literal `>=` stays as typed. Opt into the symbol
conversion with `"all"` (or `"relational"`), or turn everything off with
`"none"`:

```{r markup}
df_rel <- data.frame(Criterion = c("Age >= 65", "CrCl < 30"), n = c("120", "8"))

rtftable(df_rel)                       # default: ">=" stays literal
rtftable(df_rel, markup = "all")       # ">=" -> the >= symbol, ^{}/_{} too
rtftable(df_rel, markup = "none")      # no markup at all (everything literal)
```


## Figures

Figures are content too: one figure per page, added with `rtf_figures()`. Pass a
list of **plot objects** (a ggplot2 plot, a grid grob, a function that draws --
see the [figures article](figures.html)), image paths (PNG/JPEG), or
`rtfplot()` objects; `width_twips` / `height_twips` / `align` control the
display, and `titles` / `footnotes` work exactly as for tables.

```{r figure-object, eval = FALSE}
rtf_figures(list(ggplot(dat, aes(week, mean)) + geom_line()))  # no file needed
```

**By default a figure embeds at its native size (100%)** -- the pixel dimensions
divided by the image's own DPI (read from the PNG `pHYs` chunk / JPEG JFIF
density). A 2500 x 1438 px plot saved at 300 DPI therefore appears at
2500/300 x 1438/300 in. If the file carries no DPI, the
`rtfreporter.figure.default_dpi` option (96) is assumed. Save your graphics
device at the resolution you want on the page:

```{r figure}
# Save at 300 DPI so the native size is predictable.
img <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
png(img, width = 2500, height = 1438, res = 300)
plot(1:10, main = "Mean over time"); dev.off()

doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_figures(list(img), align = "center",           # native size (~8.3 x 4.8 in)
              titles = list(c("Figure 14.2.1", "Mean over time")))
length(doc$contents)        # one figure page
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "ac_figure.rtf")
.shot("ac_figure.png")
```

Pass an explicit `width_twips` (the height then follows the aspect ratio) to
scale a figure -- for example to shrink one that is wider than the page, since
the native size is **not** auto-capped to the writable width:

```{r figure-scale, eval = FALSE}
rtf_figures(list(img), width_twips = 9000L)          # force 6.25 in wide
```

Tables and figures share the same page model, so a report is just a sequence of
content pages -- some tables, some figures -- each optionally titled and
footnoted. To control the running header/footer across those pages, see the
headers & footers article.

## Two contents on one page

`page_break = FALSE` puts a content under the one before it, on the page that
one ends on; `space_before` adds empty lines between them. Each keeps its own
title and footnote, and is drawn exactly as it would be on a page of its own.
`rtf_layout()` (or `print(doc)`) shows the printed pages:

```{r same-page}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(df1, titles = "Table 1", footnotes = "Mean and SD.") |>
  rtf_tables(df2, titles = "Table 2", page_break = FALSE, space_before = 1)
rtf_layout(doc)
```

Nothing is measured: a content that does not fit is carried to the next page by
the reader (Word, LibreOffice). To go on with a long table on pages of its own,
say how many of its rows the shared page takes with `first_rows`; the rest is
paginated by its own `max_rows`. `rtf_figures(page_break = FALSE)` puts a
figure under a table the same way.

See `?rtf_tables` and `?rtf_figures` for the full argument reference.
